A01.evidence: A separate short, almost horizontal arch is plainly present over the e after d. Its direction does not securely distinguish grave from acute; the unaccented candidate is excluded. Final s has a downturned terminal.

A02.location: Opening line, quotation marks around modèles

A02.reading: Two opening and two closing ticks
A02.evidence: Each side has two separate short near-vertical strokes; no angle-shaped guillemets are drawn.

A03.evidence: The detached accent over the first e is a compact near-vertical dark mark. An accent is present, but its grave/acute direction cannot be distinguished securely. The f, looped l, c, high h and terminal e are visible.

A04.evidence: Half a shows the successive mono/mor humps, p descender, tall h, dotted i, q descender and joined terminal ue. The ending is readable without a further crop.

A05.evidence: The short canceled group has a initial loop, low u, tall t, small o and final m humps. The stroke ends after that short group; no morphisme sequence survives. No separate terminal stop is visible apart from the deletion stroke.

A06.evidence: Above the strike are a looped e, low n and high d with a right tail; the adjacent blank contains no detached stop.

A07.evidence: A long descending p is followed by a very compressed low a stroke and a separate right-curled r. The visible short group supports par; no abbreviation expansion is introduced.

A08.location: Definition of tilde D, quotation marks around inclusion
A08.evidence: Half a shows two small opening strokes before inclusion and two closing strokes before the parenthesis, with no angled chevrons.

A09.location: Definition of tilde D, first sous objets
A09.evidence: There is a blank gap between sous and objets. The later occurrence below the map has a visible separate hyphen; this first occurrence does not.

A10.location: End of identification sentence, before Soient
A10.evidence: The final tilded D has its own long baseline; the following blank carries no independent period before the new Soient line.

A11.C: Two rows; M directly below Hom; label at left
A11.H: Both maps in one row, comma between; M as ordinary subscript
A11.reading: Two rows; M directly below Hom; label at left
A11.evidence: Hom(D′,D) points right to tilde D on the upper row. M is directly underneath Hom. The lower row begins u, has a vertical initial bar on its rightward arrow, and ends u(D′). The star label sits separately at the left between row levels. No comma separates the two rows.

A12.evidence: The first closing delimiter has a strong horizontal upper return, upright middle and lower left return, making a bracket reading preferable. The opening delimiter is more curved/oblique, so round parentheses remain possible. The following (ii) and comma are clear.

A13.location: Image description, l’ens before canceled fragment
A13.evidence: The final s ends in a connected downturned stroke; the gap before the canceled fragment contains no separate point.

A14.location: Immediately after l’ens, small canceled fragment
A14.evidence: A very small crossed group retains a small upper counter, a larger lower counter and a rightward terminal. These permit de, but the overstroke obscures the letter junction. The doubt is retained; no word count is invented.

A15.location: Principal symbol in the image subset
A15.evidence: A completely closed oval is bisected by a central upright that continues down to a projecting horizontal foot. Both halves of the oval are visible. This is Phi rather than an open script-L loop. D has one prime in the subscript; the argument is plain D.

A16.location: Small M- and leader beneath Phi / before isomorphes
A16.C: M inserted below the subset symbol; no M- before isomorphes
A16.evidence: The small M is followed by a distinct horizontal hyphen. A curved oblique leader descends from beside it to the gap immediately before isomorphes. The M- is an insertion attached to that word, not a second index below Phi.

A17.evidence: The N has one ascending left stroke, one diagonal and one long right stroke. There is no second separated stem. The crossed glyph to its right is a separate character.

A18.location: Canceled character immediately after that N
A18.evidence: Under the crossing zigzags, a long top bar, a central upright and a long bottom bar remain. The diagonals form the cancellation; no separate K branches are needed for the underlying glyph.

A19.evidence: The s ends as a low joined wave. There is no independent point between it and the insertion attachment for préordonné.

A20.evidence: The word stands above the line. A low curved attachment leads into the space between l’ens and des. There are no paired punctuation parentheses enclosing the word.

A21.evidence: The close view has an open c joined to a tall l and low a loop, followed by compressed double-s contours and a low terminal es group. The whole sequence is readable as classes.

A22.evidence: Half b shows the sentence above Pour, attached after the point following M. Ordonné has its own straight underline. Crop 10 shows the g descender, r/a group, separate curved circumflex and ce terminal in grâce. The sentence ends with a point after (ii). The note is manuscript text, not just editorial commentary.

A24.evidence: Half b shows a separated extra upright/return beside the left stem, with projecting upper and lower bars and the diagonal/right stem still visible. This occurrence is doubled, unlike the N after Soit.

A25.location: Canceled letter between un and objet
A25.evidence: The crossed character retains an upper loop and a lower loop with a rightward foot; two diagonals cross it. The lower loop permits e, while the surviving double curvature also permits s. It is not safely resolved to either letter.

A26.C: Deleted D followed by live M
A26.H: Deleted M, with no live replacement
A26.reading: Deleted D followed by live M
A26.evidence: The composite has the curved outer bowl and projecting baseline of D, crossed by an oblique stroke. A superposed M has two high uprights and a low central return. Both contours are retained, with M as the live replacement.

A27.location: Small mark above n after classe
A27.evidence: The detached upper mark has several joined projections: a short upright, a right upper prong, a transverse connection and a lower-left projection. It is not a single prime tick. It sits over the n rather than at the usual far-right prime position.

A28.location: First à isom unique près, abbreviation ending
A28.evidence: The word at the right edge ends in the final m stroke; the remaining gap before the next-line unique has no separate point.

A29.location: After first unique près, phrase before donc
A29.evidence: The initial à is compressed to a detached accent and a low small body, as elsewhere on this page. The next word has the open c, closed a, low u and terminal se contours of cause. Half b shows the following short de and a comma after (ii). There is no comme dans sequence.

A30.location: Below the gap between à and cause
A30.reading: Small isolated down-right stroke, represented literally below the gap
A30.evidence: Crop 15 contains one detached, dark oblique stroke below and to the right of the compact à, before the following tilde-D line. It is distinct from the tilde. No linguistic or mathematical role is assigned.

A31.location: Before the defining equality, l’ens ordonné
A31.evidence: Half b shows no independent point after the final s, before ordonné.

A32.location: Right side of tilde D_n equals
A32.evidence: The complete symbol has a long projecting top bar, separated returning stems and a lower curve that turns left and upward. The leftward hook distinguishes J from a straight-foot I; the interior returning contours establish doubling. The following subscript is n. The left D also has a small flattened n joined to its baseline.

A33.evidence: Half b shows the tall d, separate accent on e, high f with descender, dotted i, low n and final dotted i. The joined middle does not hide a competing letter sequence.

A34.location: Second à isom unique près, abbreviation ending
A34.evidence: The second isom ends in a long connected m stroke, with blank space afterward; no detached abbreviation point is visible before the next-line unique.

A35.location: Canceled words before live une famille
A35.evidence: The first canceled word has a long initial descender, a tall closed second loop, a low u-like turn and a final short upright with a detached dot above it. This supports plui as the literal first candidate, while plus remains possible if the dot is incidental. Choisi is not supported by the initial contour. A comma and the old une are also crossed; a separate une is written above the old une. The horizontal strike crosses the whole old group.

A36.evidence: Half b shows the long initial f, joined a/m group, i point, two tall l contours and the terminal e stroke. The cancellation belongs to the preceding old phrase, not the live word.

A37.evidence: The family symbol has a top bar, two separated main contours and a large lower hook turning up to the left. There is no D bowl or separate tilde. The index n, the parentheses, and the lower n membership doubled N are all visible. This is independently clear at this occurrence.

A38.evidence: The terminal s has its own downstroke; the wide gap before ordonnés has no independent point.

A39.evidence: Half b shows the initial i point, joined n, high d, crossed x, separate acute stroke over e and terminal s. The plural ending is visible.

B01.evidence: The complete word has m/o/d/e/l/e/s contours. A separate short nearly horizontal accent is certainly present above the first e, excluding the unaccented candidate; its polarity remains weak. Both quotation pairs consist of two separate short strokes, not guillemets.

B02.evidence: The repeated low monomor arches, descending p, tall h, dotted i, descending q and terminal ue can be followed in half a; the word is not physically unreadable.

B03.evidence: A short a/u/t/o/m sequence occupies the crossed space. There are no further letter bodies for orphisme. The terminal dark nub touches the cancellation rule, so an independent abbreviation stop cannot be established or excluded.

B04.evidence: Raised e-n-d appears directly above the crossed abbreviation. The last d has an oval and upright with a rightward exit; the space after that exit is clear and has no separate stop.

B05.evidence: The crop shows the long descending and returning p, a reduced separate middle stroke, and the final small bent r before the spaced un. This is sufficient to read par without an in-place doubt.

B06.location: Definition of tilde D, first sous objets
B06.evidence: There is a blank gap between sous and objets. It lacks the short horizontal stroke that is visibly present at the later occurrence.

B07.location: Definition of tilde D, quoted inclusion
B07.evidence: Each flank of inclusion is a pair of short detached ticks. No angular guillemet is drawn.

B08.location: End of identification sentence, final tilde D
B08.evidence: The interlinear D with separate tilde ends the sentence spatially; there is no independent full stop to its right. The nearby point above-left belongs to the earlier D sentence, not this endpoint.

B09.C: Two rows, M directly below Hom, no comma after tilde D
B09.H: One row with Hom_M, comma after tilde D, followed by u mapsto
B09.evidence: Hom and its lower M are vertically separated. The object arrow is on the upper row and the u mapsto row lies below; the lower arrow begins with a vertical bar. The target D has a separate tilde and no trailing comma. The (*) label sits at the left.

B10.evidence: The first left enclosure is curved/slanted with a low inward turn; its right enclosure has an especially clear leftward horizontal top and a lower foot, producing a bracket-like right side. A literal mixed (i] is therefore retained ahead of the two conventional alternatives. The following (ii) has two dots and rounded enclosing strokes.

B11.location: Central paragraph, l’ens before cancelled word
B11.evidence: The s ends with its own descending hook. The intervening space before the small crossed word contains no separate abbreviation point.

B12.location: Central paragraph, small crossed word after l’ens
B12.evidence: A compact loop, a possible ascending start and a short e-like lower exit remain visible through the cancellation. They support de, but the overlapping dark strokes do not settle both letters. The C doubt is retained, not silently resolved.

B13.evidence: Half b shows a closed upper oval divided by a full central upright which continues to a wide horizontal foot. The two-sided oval is distinct from a one-sided script-L loop. The subscript is D followed by a separate prime. This resolves the alphabet as Phi on this page alone.

B14.evidence: The M has an explicit short hyphen to its right. A long curved attachment descends from just after that hyphen to the space immediately before the i of isomorphes. It does not terminate at the subset letter. H has the correct lexical prefix but does not mark its added state.

B15.location: Lower definition, live N after Soit
B15.evidence: The live N has one left upright, one descending diagonal and one returning right upright. There is no separate inner returning stem such as appears in the later N forms.

B16.location: Lower definition, cancelled letter after live N
B16.evidence: The crop separates an upright joining full top and bottom horizontal serifs from the diagonal zigzag cancellation. The I skeleton is continuous; apparent K arms belong to the zigzag.

B17.evidence: The visible abbreviation ends in its low final hook without a detached dot before des/the interlinear addition.

B18.evidence: Préordonné is written above the gap after l’ens; its long bent attachment enters the gap before des. There are no pair of round parentheses enclosing the word.

B19.evidence: The crop shows open c, tall looped l, the small a body at its foot, low repeated medial bends, and the long terminal es exit. These establish classes despite the fast reduced ending.

B20.location: End of lower defining sentence, M followed by a point
B20.evidence: A detached low dark point is visible to the right of the M, before the interlinear sentence attaches. It is separate from the right stem of M.

B21.H: \note{il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii) — l’incise est interlinéaire}
B21.evidence: Half b permits the complete Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii). The g has a descending return, followed by r and the accented middle body, then the short ce exit. A separate straight line under ordonné is deliberate underlining. The large curving line attaches the whole insertion to the point after M. H describes it in an editorial note but does not transcribe it as an insertion or preserve the underline.

B22.evidence: There are two near-uprights, a horizontal crossbar and a continuous rising diagonal joining the lower left to the upper right. The right upright also continues down below the crossbar. The extra continuation leaves the forall/H identity unresolved; no mathematical expectation was used to remove the alternative.

B23.location: First membership N in Pour n in N
B23.evidence: Half b shows a separate inner returning stroke and projecting bars in the N after membership, unlike the plain N after Soit. The doubled form is resolved at this occurrence.

B24.location: Cancelled ending of un before objet
B24.evidence: The lower surviving letter body has a small enclosed counter followed by a rightward exit, forming e. The taller upper loop and crossing diagonals are the cancellation strokes. There is no separate surviving s contour comparable to the final s elsewhere.

B25.location: After D_n de, overwritten D and live M
B25.evidence: The older broad D bowl and baseline remain beneath the two peaked strokes of a live M. The live letter is retained, and the readable underlying D is recorded before it. H both names the crossed letter differently and loses the replacement.

B26.location: Small mark immediately above classe n
B26.evidence: The mark is a compact crossed cluster with more than one short upper projection and a lower-left foot. It is not a single detached slanted prime. It sits directly above n, not to the upper right. Asterisk is a typographic approximation of this small crossed form.

B27.location: First à isom unique près, abbreviation after déterminé
B27.evidence: The final low m stroke is followed by a line break; there is no independent abbreviation point. The next line starts unique.

B28.location: After unique près, accented/colon-like cluster and detached low stroke
B28.evidence: Two small vertically separated oblique ticks occupy the place read as à in C. No open a bowl survives, so colon remains an ink alternative. A third, distinctly longer down-right stroke sits lower and to the right in the gap before cause; it is preserved as a small lowered backslash without assigning a mathematical role. The three marks are not three equal round dots.

B29.location: Words following the uncertain à/colon-like cluster
B29.evidence: The first word has open c, a closed a, a low u and short terminal se. The following word is the short d-e sequence visible in half b, not the longer dans. The repeated (ii) has two dotted uprights.

B30.location: Lower line, l’ens ordonné before equation
B30.evidence: The abbreviated ens ends in a low horizontal exit; no separate stop appears before ordonné.

B31.evidence: The full right letter has separated returning stems/white channels, a long top bar and a curved bottom that returns to the left and rises into a hook. These are doubled J contours, rather than a plain I with a straight bottom serif. The lower n is visible to its right; the equality has two separate bars.

B32.evidence: Half b shows the initial d, the separate acute stroke, a long descending f, dotted i, reduced n and final i. The letters are joined but recoverable.

B33.location: Second à isom unique près, after défini
B33.evidence: The last m exits into the blank at the right of the row. There is no independent stop before the next row unique près. The actual period follows près.

B34.location: Cancelled words before live une famille
B34.evidence: The first crossed word begins with a long descender and a tall looped l; this excludes choisi. Its small later bodies remain merged into the rule, so plus is retained as a doubtful reading. A low comma-like nub follows. The old une is readable under the same deletion line, and a second une is clearly raised above it. The rule reaches the initial f but does not cancel the following whole famille.

B35.location: Final prose line before displayed family, famille
B35.evidence: Half b shows the full descending f, following a/m/i bodies, two tall l strokes and the rightward final e. The cancellation from the earlier words is not a cancellation of famille.

B36.evidence: The main family letter has a top bar, separated descending strokes and a distinct leftward rising bottom hook, agreeing with doubled J on its own ink. No D bowl or tilde is present. The family is on its own line, with n in doubled N written as the lower indexing group.

B37.evidence: No independent dot follows ens; ordonnés follows after a space. The comma is after ordonnés.

B38.evidence: The i dot, ascending d, crossed x, short accented e and terminal s hook can be distinguished in half b. The word is indexés, including the final s.

C01.evidence: The m/o/d/e/l/e/s contours are present and the final s has a downward hook. A separate short nearly horizontal accent lies over the first e; an unaccented spelling is not supported, but its grave/acute direction remains indeterminate. Both quotation pairs are two separated ticks, not guillemets.

C02.evidence: The half shows the complete mono-morph- sequence, the tall h, dotted i, descending q and final joined ue. No terminal punctuation appears. The C doubt is resolved.

C03.evidence: An initial a oval, low u, tall t, and the following o/m humps remain under one horizontal strike. The word ends there; no further morphisme sequence or separate abbreviation point is visible.

C04.evidence: The raised replacement has e, n and the tall round-backed d; the blank after d contains no separate point.

C05.evidence: A long narrow descending p-like loop is followed by a very short horizontal body and a separate small hooked ending. These permit par, but the a/r bodies are too reduced for a confident resolution. C doubt retained.

C06.evidence: There is a blank between sous and objets at the first occurrence. The later occurrence has an actual short horizontal hyphen, checked independently in half b.

C07.evidence: Two short ticks open and two short ticks close the word; no angle-shaped guillemets are drawn.

C08.evidence: After the last tilded D of the paragraph there is no separate full stop. Its detached upper mark is the tilde, not punctuation.

C09.C: Two aligned rows; M directly beneath Hom; no comma after target
C09.H: One row; Hom_M; comma after target
C09.reading: Two aligned rows; \underset{M}{\mathrm{Hom}}(D\prime,D)\to\widetilde D, then u\mapsto u(D\prime), with no source comma
C09.evidence: The Hom/M pair occupies the upper row, with M centered beneath Hom. The u-map is on a separate lower row. The upper arrow has a rightward head; the lower arrow has an initial vertical bar and a rightward head. There is no comma beside the upper target. The star label lies at the left between the rows. Both primes and the unprimed second Hom argument were checked.

C10.evidence: The first enclosure has pronounced short horizontal returns, especially the top and foot of the right delimiter; the inner stroke is undotted. The outer portions are also curved, so parentheses cannot be excluded. The following (ii) has two dots and curved delimiters. The bracket alternative is placed first.

C11.evidence: The last s ends in a down-hook. No separate abbreviation stop lies before the canceled cluster.

C12.evidence: The cramped canceled ink has a tiny upper counter, a larger lower loop, and a short rightward terminal. The d/e division is obscured by retracing; de remains a tentative reading rather than a resolved word.

C13.evidence: In half b the upper closed oval is bisected by a vertical stem that continues down to a separate broad horizontal foot. Both lobes are present. This is the Phi contour; the script/plain L alternatives are removed. The lower D has a detached prime.

C14.location: Interline below subset name and before isomorphes
C14.evidence: A small M is immediately followed by a short horizontal hyphen. The adjacent curved oblique leader runs down-left to the gap just before isomorphes. The insertion therefore attaches M- to that word, rather than placing M as a mathematical subscript under Phi. H has the resulting wording but does not mark its inserted state.

C15.evidence: The first N has one left stem, one descending diagonal and one long right stem, with no separated returning stem. This differs visibly from the later doubled N forms.

C16.evidence: A central upright joins a long top bar and a long bottom bar. The diagonal/zigzag strokes traverse this barred I as cancellation; no independent K arms are needed. C doubt resolved as I.

C17.evidence: There is no separate point after the small terminal s before the insertion attachment at des.

C18.evidence: The word is raised above the baseline between l’ens and des, with a curved attachment under it. The line is an insertion leader; it does not enclose the word as textual parentheses. The acute accent is separate.

C19.evidence: The enlarged word has an open c joined to a tall l, a small closed a return at its foot, a low paired ss sequence, and the flattened terminal es with a down-hook. C doubt resolved, with the medial compression noted.

C20.H: \note{il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii) — l’incise est interlinéaire}
C20.evidence: The actual ink is an interlinear sentence beginning with capital Il, attached after M. A short independent line under ordonné marks underlining, distinct from the much longer attachment rule. A comma follows ordonné and a stop follows (ii). H describes the interlinear text editorially but does not include it as manuscript insertion with its underline. The grace doubt is addressed separately.

C21.evidence: The g has an open upper bowl and long hooked descender; the following low r/a sequence has a clear small circumflex arch above a, followed by flattened ce. The separate à is represented by a compact body with an accent above, as elsewhere on the page.

C22.location: Classification sentence ending d’objets de M
C22.evidence: A distinct low full stop appears immediately after the large M before the new Pour clause.

C23.evidence: The glyph has two long outer uprights, a diagonal rising from lower-left to upper-right, and a lower-middle horizontal crossing stroke. These allow a strongly retraced universal sign but retain an H-like alternative. The full glyph does not settle the identity.

C24.location: Membership n in N after Pour
C24.evidence: In half b this N has a separate returning stem/white channel and projecting bars, unlike the first plain N. C alphabet doubt is removed. Both later N occurrences were checked separately and also have doubled strokes.

C25.location: Canceled letter between un and objet
C25.evidence: Several oblique canceling strokes cross a small lower counter and rightward terminal; an upper loop may belong to the cancellation. The lower form favors e but can also preserve the s read by H. The ink does not establish the original letter securely.

C26.evidence: The large oval bowl with a left upright and long foot belongs to D; over it are the two peaks and middle valley of a live M. Both contours are visible. H omits the live replacement and identifies the deleted contour differently.

C27.location: Detached mark over n of classe
C27.evidence: The separate small mark has more than one branch: two upper prongs and a lower-left spur connected across a dark center. It is not a single prime stroke. Asterisk is retained and prime removed; its placement is above n, not at the baseline.

C28.evidence: The first isom terminates in a continuous low horizontal tail with blank after it at the line end. No distinct abbreviation stop follows m.

C29.evidence: There are two short vertically separated marks at the left and a third detached oblique stroke below and to their right. The left pair can be the compressed accented à seen elsewhere, but the three-mark cluster also permits a therefore-like reading. The exact function of the third stroke is unsettled.

C30.location: Words between the preceding mark and (ii)
C30.evidence: The first word begins with an open c and small a loop, followed by the reduced u/s/e sequence. The following word has a looped d and a single long low e, not the extra a/n/s sequence of dans. The citation itself is (ii), followed by a comma.

C31.evidence: The right glyph has a full top bar, separated returning uprights and a broad bottom hook turning left/up. The hook is incompatible with the plain I reading. Both n indices and the two distinct equality bars are visible. C doubt resolves as doubled J.

C32.evidence: In half b the initial looped d, separate acute accent, tall f and subsequent i/n/i sequence are visible. C doubt is resolved.

C33.evidence: The second isom ends in a long low tail, with no separate stop before the following line unique près. The final stop after près is distinct and retained.

C34.location: Canceled phrase and raised une before famille
C34.evidence: The first canceled word begins with a long descending p and tall looped l; those contours do not support choisi. Its reduced ending includes a detached point and is still not fully secure, so plus remains marked. A low comma and the canceled une follow under the same stroke. A second une is written above as the live replacement. The cancellation continues into the initial f region, but the remaining famille is live.

C35.location: Final prose before displayed family, famille
C35.evidence: Half b shows the full tall f, low a/mi sequence and two tall l strokes, followed by the final e. The word is live despite the old cancellation crossing its initial region. C doubt resolved.

C36.evidence: The family is on its own line. Its capital has a strong top bar, doubled upright structure and clearly upturned left hook at the foot; it is the J form, with no D bowl and no separate tilde. Parentheses, lower n and the n-in-doubled-N index are present.

C37.evidence: No separate point occurs after ens. The comma is after ordonnés and is kept.

C38.evidence: The i stroke, tall d, crossed x and short rising acute above the later e can be followed in half b; the final s is a small hooked ending. C doubt resolved.
